latest.title: Likkutei Sichos: Sukkos
latest.blurb: The festival of Sukkos is named after the sukkah because it is the mitzvah that encompasses the entire person from the very start of Yom Tov, enabling us to elevate even our most ordinary activities into Divine service throughout the year. The incomparable joy of Simchas Beis Hashoevah comes from transcending our usual boundaries, as even the highest human faculty—the intellect—finds its fulfillment in submitting to what lies beyond reason. new.title: Samach Vav Part 222:  We invoke the angels' passion to impact the animal soul, rooted in the angels
new.blurb: Samach Vav p. 182-183: Why do we need to invoke the angels (in the blessings before Shema) to appreciate the greatness of the Divine, especially considering that souls are greater than angels, so why do we get excited by the angels' excitement? Answer: Invoking the angels' praise and love is to impact the animal soul, which stems from these angels. The angels' excitement results from their contemplation about the source and manner of their creation (in addition to them being created from a mere reflection). This contemplation consists of the following: The Divine creation of existence is fundamentally different from a man-made creation, which essentially consists of reshaping an existing entity (yesh m'yesh), not a creation of existence from non-existence (yesh m'ayin). As such, a man-made product, though the producer applies himself to producing the product and his power manifests in the product, yet after the product is produced, it is a separate, self-contained entity and is no longer in need of the producer, since it was an existent entity (in its raw form) even before it was reshaped by the producer. Vice versa as well: The very raw matter of the product, as well as its reshaped state and the benefit and function of this newly shaped product, does not exist within the power of the producer.

new.blurb: Samach Vav p. 182 [Beginning of discourse 17:] Questions: 1. Why does it say Vayeilech Ish? 2. What is the meaning of the Zohar explaining this verse, that she was diminished by song, and he came to elevate her? 3. What are the three expressions used? To reach ahava rabba one first needs the avodah pnimiyus of the mind and heart, and of refining the animal soul. Prayer refines the animal soul with the fire below, the fire above that relates to the animal soul, and the fire above that relates to the divine soul. We explained that the fire below is Pesukei D'zimrah -- the contemplation on the awesome power of creation, which ignites the soul's fiery passion. We will now explain the fire above that relates to the animal soul: The animal soul is rooted in the angels above, the animals in the divine chariot. Thus, contemplating the bittul of the angels in the blessings before the Shema -- how they are ablaze with fiery passion to be subsumed and absorbed in the Divine energy within them -- this contemplation impacts the power of desire (koach ha'misaveh) of the animal soul, which originates in these angels, to redirect its love and passion for material pleasures to a love and passion for G-dliness.

new.title: Samach Vav Part 220: The stages of prayer ignite the fire below and above to refine the animal soul

This contemplation ignites the soul's passion (a person gets excited when he experiences renewal), which elevates and uplifts his spirit above the crassness of the mundane. This is followed by the blessings before the Shema – the fire from above that elevates the animal soul, and then the Shema – the fire from above of the Divine soul, which utterly consumes the animal soul (as will be discussed later). And then he receives his reward from above -- ahava rabba in Shemone Esreih. Vice versa as well: The very raw matter of the product, as well as its reshaped state and the benefit and function of this newly shaped product, does not exist within the power of the producer.
